title: Normalize embed + rerank iterator contract and graceful-degradation playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Multiple client SDKs and first-party integrations expect a stable cursor/iterator and error semantics from both embeddings and rerank endpoints. Recent runtime changes introduced differences in streaming shapes, structured result envelopes, and transient vs. terminal error codes between /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank. This has caused a class of consumer bugs: iterator duplication, infinite polling loops, and opaque fallback behavior in downstream services.

Goal: Define a single compatibility contract and migration playbook that: (1) normalizes pagination/cursor semantics across embed + rerank; (2) establishes a small, deterministic error taxonomy with mapped HTTP codes and retry semantics; (3) documents streaming interaction edge cases (structured outputs and tool-calling hooks) for backcompat clients; and (4) provides an ops + migration rollout plan with observability checks and automatic graceful-degradation rules for runtime.

Why now: Increasing Dedicated and Private deployments are surfacing edgecases where small differences between endpoints cause customer-visible regressions. Unifying the contract reduces client-surface churn and enables safer automated fallbacks in Console routing rules.
acceptance_criteria: Specification published to Confluence: 'Embed+Rerank API Compatibility Contract' with examples for cursor formation and canonical pagination headers
Server-side adapter implemented that translates legacy cursor tokens to canonical form for both endpoints (can be toggled via feature flag)
Error mapping implemented: transient vs terminal codes documented and emitted consistently with guidance for client retries
Streaming envelopes standardized: when structured outputs (JSON tool/tool-calls) appear mid-stream, downstream iterators receive consistent boundary markers
Integration tests covering: cursor round-trip, truncated/partial pages, duplicate cursor handling, and retry semantics (ENG test suite + CI)
Monitoring dashboards: percent of legacy-cursor hits, retry rates per client library, and customer-facing incidents reduced by 75% in first two weeks post-rollout
tasks: Draft initial spec and compatibility table (owner: PM) - Confluence draft link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/EmbedRerank+Compatibility
Align on canonical cursor format (opaque token with version prefix + checksum) and header mappings (owner: ENG) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4876
Define error taxonomy and idempotency/retry guidance for clients (owner: PM + ENG)
Adapter implementation behind feature flag that serves canonical cursors for legacy clients (owner: ENG)
Update SDKs (python/js/go) to handle canonical cursor + well-defined retry hints (owner: DevEx)
Create test matrix for partial-page streaming + structured outputs (owner: QA)
Canary rollout plan and rollback criteria (owner: SRE)
Customer comms draft and migration notes for top 10 customers (owner: CS)
Post-launch evaluation and follow-up buglist (owner: PM)
rollout_plan:
1) Publish spec and run a 48h review with ENG/DevEx/QA. 2) Deliver adapter behind feature flag; run internal e2e tests. 3) Canary to 5% traffic for 72h; monitor retry counts, duplicate-iterator errors, and latency. 4) Expand to 50% for 7 days, then full rollout if metrics stable. 5) Coordinate SDK releases: JS patch within canary window, Python patch before 50% expansion.

Rollback triggers: >2x increase in client retry rate, >1% customer-visible error spike tied to cursor parsing, or any regression in top-20 endpoint latency percentiles.
api_compat_mapping: Canonical cursor: v2-{base64(payload)} where payload includes endpoint id, sequence offset, and 8-byte checksum. Legacy cursor shapes: numeric offset, 'next_cursor' tokens, and link-header iterators will be mapped server-side. Pagination headers: prefer 'X-Redwood-Next-Cursor' and maintain Link header for legacy clients. For streaming: stream frames where 'frame_type' is one of [meta,data,tool-call,end]. Structured outputs must be emitted as a single 'data' frame with content-type 'application/json+rdw' to avoid mid-stream boundary ambiguity. Clients receiving 'meta' frames should treat them as non-terminal and do not advance cursor until an 'end' frame or explicit per-page 'boundary' marker is received.
monitoring: Dashboards: 'EmbedRerank: Cursor Errors' (counts of bad_cursor, cursor_collision, duplicate_page), 'EmbedRerank: Retry Signals' (429/503 rates by client), 'Streaming Frame Integrity' (frame_type parity, incomplete_streams). Alerts: P0 alert if bad_cursor ratio >0.5% of requests for two consecutive 10m windows or if duplicate-page rate increases >200% during canary. Logging: attach request-id, feature-flag state, and parsed cursor provenance to every error to speed triage.
notes: Design tradeoffs considered: opaque canonical token (simple, versioned) vs structured JSON cursor (easier debugging but brittle across SDKs). We selected opaque token to minimize client parsing changes.
Edgecase: when streaming and structured tool-calls are used, some SDKs buffered by line can break JSON boundaries; enforcement of explicit frame markers recommended
Related work: Console routing will use the canonical token's endpoint id to select optimized rerank models per customer under Dedicated
